title: Cohere Research Intelligence (CRI) Demo & Benchmark Questions
target_paper: 1810.04805v2.pdf (BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding)

questions.question: What does BERT stand for?
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes that BERT stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, citing the Abstract or Section 1.

questions.question: What are the two model sizes introduced for BERT?
questions.expected_behavior: Details BERT_BASE (12 layers, 768 hidden, 12 heads, 110M parameters) and BERT_LARGE (24 layers, 1024 hidden, 16 heads, 340M parameters), citing Section 3.

questions.question: What corpora were used to pre-train BERT?
questions.expected_behavior: Identifies the BooksCorpus (800M words) and English Wikipedia (2,500M words), citing Section 3.1.

questions.question: What activation function is used in BERT's intermediate feed-forward layers?
questions.expected_behavior: Identifies the GELU (Gaussian Error Linear Unit) activation function, citing Section 3.

questions.question: What maximum sequence length was used during pre-training?
questions.expected_behavior: Notes pre-training used sequence length 128 for 90% of steps and sequence length 512 for the remaining 10% of steps to learn positional embeddings, citing Section 3.1.

questions.question: What is Masked Language Modeling in BERT?
questions.expected_behavior: Explains that 15% of token positions are chosen at random: 80% replaced with [MASK], 10% replaced with a random token, and 10% kept unchanged, trained to predict the original token via cross-entropy loss, citing Section 3.1.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)?
questions.expected_behavior: Explains the binary classification task where 50% of pairs are consecutive sentences (IsNext) and 50% are randomly paired (NotNext) to capture inter-sentence relationships for QA and NLI, citing Section 3.1.

questions.question: What are the three main contributions of this paper?
questions.expected_behavior: Enumerates the 3 contributions: demonstrating importance of bidirectional pre-training, showing pre-trained representations eliminate need for heavily engineered architectures, and advancing SOTA on 11 NLP tasks, citing Section 1.

questions.question: What results did BERT achieve on GLUE and SQuAD?
questions.expected_behavior: Reports GLUE score of 80.5% (BERT_BASE: 79.6%, BERT_LARGE: 80.5%), SQuAD v1.1 F1 of 93.2, and SQuAD v2.0 F1 of 83.1, citing Section 4.1 and Section 4.2.

questions.question: How does BERT represent input sequences containing two sentences?
questions.expected_behavior: Explains concatenation into a single sequence with [CLS] token at start, [SEP] token separating sentences, and learned segment embeddings (EA and EB) added to token and position embeddings, citing Section 3.

questions.question: What is the difference between BERT's fine-tuning and feature-based approaches?
questions.expected_behavior: Contrasts fine-tuning (updating all BERT parameters end-to-end for downstream tasks) with feature-based approaches (extracting fixed activations from intermediate/top layers without updating BERT weights), citing Section 4.3 and Section 5.3.

questions.question: How does BERT differ from OpenAI GPT and ELMo in directionality?
questions.expected_behavior: Clarifies that BERT uses deep bidirectional self-attention across all layers, whereas OpenAI GPT uses left-to-right unidirectional self-attention, and ELMo trains shallow left-to-right and right-to-left LSTMs independently and concatenates them, citing Section 1 and Section 2.

questions.question: Compare BERT_BASE and BERT_LARGE in terms of layers, hidden size, attention heads, and parameter count.
questions.expected_behavior: Compares BERT_BASE (L=12, H=768, A=12, 110M params) with BERT_LARGE (L=24, H=1024, A=16, 340M params), noting BERT_LARGE was chosen to match OpenAI GPT's model size for direct architectural comparison, citing Section 3.

questions.question: What is the population of Mars?
questions.expected_behavior: Triggers safe abstention via Evidence Sufficiency Gate. Returns refusal stating insufficient evidence in the selected document. Zero hallucinated figures.

questions.question: According to the paper, what is Medusa decoding and how many speculative heads does it use?
questions.expected_behavior: Triggers safe abstention. The system recognizes that Medusa decoding is not discussed in the BERT paper, refusing rather than guessing from pre-trained weights.

questions.question: What learning rate did the authors use when training BERT on Llama-3 checkpoints?
questions.expected_behavior: Triggers safe abstention. Detects that the question assumes entities (Llama-3) not present in the document evidence, returning safe insufficient-evidence notification.

questions.question: What are the two pre-training tasks in BERT, and what does each task do?
questions.expected_behavior: Assembles multi-hop evidence from Section 3.1 covering both Task #1 (Masked Language Modeling: random token masking and prediction) and Task #2 (Next Sentence Prediction: binary sentence adjacency classification).

questions.question: Why does BERT pre-training use 80% [MASK], 10% random token, and 10% original token instead of 100% [MASK]?
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes the rationale from Section 3.1 explaining that the [MASK] token never appears during downstream fine-tuning; the 80/10/10 distribution mitigates pre-train/fine-tune mismatch and forces the encoder to maintain a continuous contextual representation for every input token.
